Smoothed Empirical Hazard by Treatment Arm

Source: R/estimate_empirical_hazard.R
estimate_empirical_hazard.Rd

Estimates the hazard function of each treatment arm without a parametric assumption with bshazard::bshazard(), which smooths the hazard with B-splines whose smoothness is estimated from the data through a Poisson generalised linear mixed model (Rebora et al., 2014).

Usage

estimate_empirical_hazard(
  data,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  nbin = NULL,
  nk = 31,
  degree = 1
)

Arguments

data

Data frame returned by processing_dataset.

conf_level

Confidence level of the pointwise intervals, a single number in (0, 1). The default is 0.95.

nbin

Number of time intervals in which the data are split, passed to bshazard::bshazard(). The default NULL uses the distinct observed times.

nk

Number of knots of the B-splines. The default is 31, as in bshazard::bshazard().

degree

Degree of the B-splines. The default is 1, as in bshazard::bshazard().

Value

A data frame with the columns ARM, time, hazard, lcl and ucl. Rows with a non-finite hazard are removed.

References

Rebora P, Salim A, Reilly M (2014). bshazard: A flexible tool for nonparametric smoothing of the hazard function. The R Journal 6(2):114-122. doi:10.32614/RJ-2014-028

Examples

raw <- generate_dummy_survival_data(
  arm = c("Control", "Treatment"), n = c(100, 100),
  hazards = log(2) / c(12, 18), dropout_per_year = 0.1, seed = 123
)
dat <- processing_dataset(raw, column_arm = "ARM",
                          column_survtime = "SURVTIME",
                          column_cnsr = "CNSR")
head(estimate_empirical_hazard(dat))
#>       ARM       time     hazard        lcl        ucl
#> 1 Control 0.07962164 0.05461771 0.04003634 0.07450965
#> 2 Control 0.50471440 0.05458969 0.04024447 0.07404828
#> 3 Control 0.54667799 0.05458692 0.04026481 0.07400339
#> 4 Control 0.54997400 0.05458671 0.04026640 0.07399987
#> 5 Control 0.72864686 0.05457494 0.04035252 0.07381011
#> 6 Control 0.73181776 0.05457473 0.04035404 0.07380676
